answer: In an agent economy, sybil attacks can be resisted by tying each agent identity to a unique relic of historical activity that serves as an immutable anchor in the global atlas of reputations. Agents must accumulate verifiable interaction history over time; new identities start with zero weight and cannot multiply influence until their relic grows through sustained, costly participation. This makes mass creation of fake agents economically unviable because forging a meaningful history requires real time and resources that cannot be parallelized easily.
